title: The Out of Reach Key
complaint: Hi! I'm Leo. I was playing in the basement playroom when the old doorknob fell off and locked me inside! The shiny metal key is sitting on the hallway floor right outside, but it's just out of reach under the door gap.
on_hand_items: a pair of sneakers with long shoelaces

clue_cards.title: Magnetic Attraction
clue_cards.insight: The key is made of metal. Is there something in the room that loves to stick to shiny metal objects?

clue_cards.title: Long Reach
clue_cards.insight: Your arm might be too short to reach under the door, but you have several long objects that can slide under the gap perfectly.

clue_cards.title: Sticky Connections
clue_cards.insight: Duct tape is great for holding things together, but if you flip it so the sticky side faces out, it can grab onto things you touch.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Magnetic Fishing Line
potential_solutions.description: Pull a long shoelace out of one of the sneakers and tie it tightly to the horseshoe magnet. Slide the magnet under the door gap, hold onto the other end of the shoelace, and swing it until it clicks onto the metal key to pull it back inside.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: The Sticky Stick
potential_solutions.description: Take the roll of duct tape and wrap a piece backward around one end of the wooden ruler so the sticky side is facing out. Slide the ruler under the door and press the sticky end down onto the key to grab it.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Mega Hook
potential_solutions.description: Pull the wire clothes hanger apart so it forms a long wire, keeping a small hook at one end. Use the duct tape to attach the straight end of the wire tightly to the broken broomstick. Slide this extra-long hook under the door to grab the key.

title: The Treehouse Trap
complaint: Hi! I'm Maya. I am trapped inside my backyard treehouse because the door handle jammed, and the metal key fell out of the window and is sitting on the grass just out of my reach!
on_hand_items: a piece of wrapped chewing gum

clue_cards.title: Magnetic Pull
clue_cards.insight: Keys are usually made of metal, which means a strong magnet will snap right onto them if it gets close enough.

clue_cards.title: Extending Your Reach
clue_cards.insight: You have several long items that can reach the ground from the window, like yarn, a jump rope, or a broom.

clue_cards.title: Sticky Trap
clue_cards.insight: Chewed gum is incredibly sticky and can easily pick up a small, light object if pressed against it.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: Direct Action
potential_solutions.description: Tie the end of the knitting yarn tightly around the horseshoe magnet. Lower the magnet out the window until it touches the metal key on the grass, then carefully pull it back up to unlock the door.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: Environmental Adaptation
potential_solutions.description: Unwrap and chew the gum until it is sticky, then press it firmly onto the bottom of the plastic bucket. Tie the jump rope to the bucket's handle, lower it down over the key, and press down so the gum grabs the key before pulling it up.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: Lateral Swap
potential_solutions.description: Bend the wire coat hanger into a hook shape. Use the roll of duct tape to securely tape the hanger to the end of the wooden broom, creating a long reaching pole to hook the key from the grass and bring it inside.

title: The Great Treehouse Trap
complaint: Hi! I'm Chloe. I'm stuck inside my backyard treehouse because the trapdoor locked behind me. The metal key ring slipped out of my hand and fell onto the grass right below the window, and it is way too far down for me to reach!
on_hand_items: a pair of sneakers with long shoelaces

clue_cards.title: Magnetic Attraction
clue_cards.insight: Magnets are great at grabbing certain metals. If you can find a way to lower a magnet to the ground, it might just grab that metal key ring for you.

clue_cards.title: Sticky Fingers
clue_cards.insight: Something sticky can be just as good as a hand. Chewed gum is surprisingly good at picking up small, light objects if you press it down firmly.

clue_cards.title: Hook, Line, and Sinker
clue_cards.insight: Sometimes you need a hook to catch your prize. Wire can easily be bent out of its normal shape to form a catching tool.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: Magnetic Fishing
potential_solutions.description: Take the long shoelaces out of the sneakers and tie them together to make a long string. Tie one end to the heavy metal horseshoe magnet, then lower it out the window until it snaps onto the metal key ring. Carefully pull it back up!

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: Sticky Drop
potential_solutions.description: Chew a piece of gum until it is really sticky, then press it onto one end of the wooden ruler. Use the masking tape to firmly attach the jump rope to the other end of the ruler. Lower the ruler down, press the gum onto the key, and lift it up.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Hanger Hook
potential_solutions.description: Bend the wire coat hanger so it forms a long straight wire with a hook at the bottom. Tie the jump rope to the top part of the wire, lower it out the window, and hook the key ring to pull it back inside.

title: The Bookshelf Trap
complaint: Hi! I'm Toby. I was looking for a video game in my older brother's room, and the door locked behind me! The spare key fell down a skinny gap behind his giant heavy bookshelf, and my arms are too short to reach it.
on_hand_items: a pair of sneakers with shoelaces

clue_cards.title: Reaching Deep
clue_cards.insight: Your arm might not fit behind the bookshelf, but something long, flat, or bendable can slide right down that narrow gap.

clue_cards.title: Sticky and Tricky
clue_cards.insight: If you can't grab the key with your fingers, maybe you can make something else grab it for you using something sticky or magnetic.

clue_cards.title: Tying it Together
clue_cards.insight: Shoelaces aren't just for shoes! If you pull them out, they make great mini-ropes to lower things down into tight spaces.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Magnetic Fisher
potential_solutions.description: Take a shoelace out of the sneakers and tie it tightly around the fridge magnet. Hold the flashlight to see down the crack, and lower the magnet on the string until it catches the metal key and pulls it up.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: The Sticky Stick
potential_solutions.description: Wrap some clear tape around the end of the wooden ruler, making sure the sticky side is facing out. Slide the ruler down the gap behind the bookshelf and press it firmly against the key to stick it and lift it out.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Wire Hook
potential_solutions.description: Bend the wire clothes hanger so it stretches out into a long piece of wire, leaving a small hook at the very end. Slide the wire hook down the gap, loop it through the key ring, and carefully pull the key back up.

title: The Hallway Key Rescue

on_hand_items: a pair of sneakers with long shoelaces

clue_cards.title: Sticky Reach
clue_cards.insight: The gap under the door is very narrow. Is there something long and flat you can use, maybe combined with something sticky to grab the key?

clue_cards.title: Magnetic Pull
clue_cards.insight: Keys and key rings are often made of metal that sticks to magnets. How can you slide a magnet far enough under the door to reach it?

clue_cards.title: Hook and Pull
clue_cards.insight: Sometimes you just need to hook the key ring. You might be able to bend a long piece of metal to catch the ring and drag it back.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Sticky Stick
potential_solutions.description: Wrap some masking tape around the end of the wooden ruler with the sticky side facing out. Slide the ruler under the door gap, press the sticky tape onto the key, and carefully slide it back to you.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: Fishing for Keys
potential_solutions.description: Take a long shoelace out of the sneakers and tie it securely around the heavy fridge magnet. Slide the magnet under the door gap, wiggle the shoelace until the magnet clicks onto the metal key, and pull it back into the room.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Wire Hook
potential_solutions.description: Unwind the wire clothes hanger and straighten it out, bending just the very tip to create a small hook. Slide the wire under the door, catch the loop of the key ring, and drag the key back to your side.

setting: An old, dimly lit office during a corporate retreat
title: The Grate Mistake
complaint: Hi! I'm Zoe. I'm locked inside an old, dimly lit office during my company's supposedly fun escape room retreat, and the actual brass key to the exit just slipped out of my hand and fell down a narrow, heavy cast-iron floor grate that I can't lift.
on_hand_items: a pair of sneakers with long shoelaces

clue_cards.title: Clue 1: Material Matters
clue_cards.insight: Brass keys are not magnetic, so a magnet won't stick to the key itself, but the metal ring attached to the key might be made of steel.

clue_cards.title: Clue 2: Sticky Alternatives
clue_cards.insight: If magnetism fails, a strong adhesive or sticky substance can latch onto almost any small, lightweight object.

clue_cards.title: Clue 3: Rigid vs. Flexible Reach
clue_cards.insight: A dangling string can be hard to aim through a narrow space. A rigid object gives you better control to push down directly onto the target.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Sticky Stick
potential_solutions.description: Wrap duct tape around the end of the wooden yardstick with the sticky side facing out. Use the flashlight to see down the grate, then carefully poke the yardstick through the slots to press the tape firmly against the key and lift it up.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: The Magnetic Drop
potential_solutions.description: Remove a shoelace from one of the sneakers and tie it tightly around the fridge magnet. Lower the magnet through the grate until it touches the key. If the keychain ring is steel, it will snap to the magnet, allowing you to pull it back up.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Gum Harpoon
potential_solutions.description: Chew a piece of gum until it is soft and very sticky. Unbend the wire coat hanger until it is straight, stick the chewed gum onto the very tip, and guide it down through the grate to grab the flat side of the brass key.

title: The Tube Trap
complaint: Hi! I'm Elena. I am locked inside a retro 1980s themed office escape room with only five minutes left on the clock, but the final exit key is sitting at the bottom of a narrow, transparent tube bolted to the floor and my arm can't fit inside to grab it!
on_hand_items: a pair of sneakers with long shoelaces

clue_cards.title: Clue 1: Extend Your Reach
clue_cards.insight: If your hand won't fit into the narrow space, you need to find an item that is long and rigid, or something flexible that can be lowered all the way to the bottom.

clue_cards.title: Clue 2: The Attraction Factor
clue_cards.insight: Standard keys are often made of brass, which means a magnet won't pick them up. You will need to rely on something sticky or a physical hook.

clue_cards.title: Clue 3: Reshaping Metal
clue_cards.insight: Sometimes everyday items can be bent out of their original shape to serve a completely new purpose.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Sticky Stick
potential_solutions.description: Unroll a piece of the sticky tape and wrap it around one end of the wooden ruler so the sticky side is facing outward. Reach the ruler down the tube, press the tape firmly onto the key, and lift it out.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: The Gum Drop
potential_solutions.description: Remove a shoelace from the sneakers and stick the wad of chewed bubblegum securely to one end. Lower the shoelace down the tube like a fishing line until the gum hits the key, let it grip for a second, and carefully pull the key up.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Wire Hook
potential_solutions.description: Take the wire coat hanger and untwist it until you have a single, long piece of wire. Bend the very tip into a small hook, lower it down the tube, catch the ring of the key, and fish it to the top.

title: The Grate Escape
complaint: Hi! I'm Marcus. I'm locked inside this old Victorian study room trying to win a local escape room challenge, but I accidentally dropped the small brass exit key down a narrow floor grate and my fingers can't fit through the slots to reach it.
on_hand_items: a pair of dress shoes with long shoelaces

clue_cards.title: Sticky Situation
clue_cards.insight: Brass isn't magnetic, so you will need to find something that can physically grip or stick to the key without needing to tie a knot around it.

clue_cards.title: Reaching Out
clue_cards.insight: You have a few items that can be unbent, unwound, or extended to poke through small openings and reach the bottom of the grate.

clue_cards.title: Shedding Light
clue_cards.insight: It is nearly impossible to fish for a key if you can't see the bottom of the dark floor grate. A light source might help guide your aim.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: Sticky Hanger Hook
potential_solutions.description: Bend the wire coat hanger until it is a long, straight piece of metal. Chew a piece of the chewing gum to make it sticky, then press it firmly onto the end of the wire. Lower the wire down the floor grate to press the gum against the flat side of the brass key, then carefully pull it back up.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: Tape and Broom Reach
potential_solutions.description: Take a piece of duct tape and fold it over the bottom end of the wooden broom handle so the sticky side faces outward. Tape the pocket flashlight to the side of the broom handle so you can see down the grate, then push the broom handle down to stick the tape to the key.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: Shoelace Lasso
potential_solutions.description: Remove the shoelaces from the dress shoes and tie them together to make a long string. Tie a small slip knot loop at the bottom. Turn on the flashlight and lay it flat on the grate facing down to illuminate the space, then lower the shoelace loop to lasso the teeth of the brass key and pull it up.

title: The Grate Escape
complaint: Hi! I'm David. I am trapped in my basement study after the cheap doorknob completely snapped off from the inside. The only spare key to the deadbolt fell down a narrow floor grate, and I cannot reach it with my fingers!
on_hand_items: a pair of heavy duty scissors

clue_cards.title: Clue 2: Sticky Situations
clue_cards.insight: Chewing gum becomes an incredibly sticky adhesive once chewed. If attached to the end of a long, rigid object, it can pick up light items from tight spaces.

clue_cards.title: Clue 3: Bend and Hook
clue_cards.insight: Thick metal wire can be reshaped. If you cut it and bend it into a tight hook, it can snag small rings or edges that are otherwise out of reach.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: Magnetic Fishing
potential_solutions.description: Unwind a long piece of the cotton yarn and tie it securely around the heavy horseshoe magnet. Lower the magnet down through the floor grate until it clicks onto the metal key, then carefully pull it back up.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: The Sticky Pole
potential_solutions.description: Chew several pieces of the chewing gum until they are very sticky. Press the chewed gum firmly onto the very tip of the long wooden broom handle. Shine the flashlight down the grate to aim, press the gum onto the key, and slowly lift it out.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: Custom Wire Hook
potential_solutions.description: Use the heavy duty scissors to snip the metal wire coat hanger. Bend the wire into a long, straight rod with a small hook at the bottom end. Slide the wire hook through the grate, catch the ring of the key, and pull it up to freedom.

title: The High Shelf Key
complaint: Hi! I'm Hannah. I'm locked inside my eccentric uncle's study during his DIY escape room challenge, and I need to retrieve a brass key resting on a high bookshelf just out of reach.

clue_cards.title: Clue 1: Sticky Fingers

clue_cards.title: Clue 2: Hook and Pull
clue_cards.insight: Thin metal objects can be bent and reshaped into entirely new tools to snag small items.

clue_cards.title: Clue 3: Shake It Up
clue_cards.insight: If you can't reach the top of the shelf, striking the bottom of it from below might jolt the item enough to make it fall.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: Direct Action
potential_solutions.description: Wrap a few pieces of double-sided tape around one end of the wooden yardstick, reach up to the high shelf, and press the sticky end against the brass key to pull it down.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: Environmental Adaptation
potential_solutions.description: Place the plastic wastebasket directly beneath the key to catch it. Then, toss the thick encyclopedia or the brass paperweight at the underside of the bookshelf to bump it, knocking the key off the ledge and into the basket.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: Lateral Swap
potential_solutions.description: Unwind and bend the wire coat hanger until it forms a long, straight rod with a hook at the end, then use it to snag the brass key and drag it off the shelf.

title: The Vanishing Key

clue_cards.title: Reach Extender

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: The Sticky Ruler
potential_solutions.description: Chew a piece of chewing gum until it is sticky. Press it onto one end of the wooden ruler, then reach the ruler down the vent and press the gum firmly onto the key to lift it out.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Wire Hook
potential_solutions.description: Pull the wire clothes hanger apart to make one long piece of wire. Leave a small hook shape at the very end, and use it to fish the key out by hooking onto its keychain ring.

title: The Missing Keys

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Paperclip Hook
potential_solutions.description: Bend the metal paperclip open so it looks like a hook. Use a piece of masking tape to attach it to the end of the wooden ruler or the dried-out marker, then reach down to hook the key ring and pull it up.

title: Talent Show Time Crunch

clue_cards.title: Reaching Out

title: The Bookcase Black Hole

title: The Airport Dash

clue_cards.insight: You have several items that can be bent into a hook or used as a fishing line to reach deep into a narrow space.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: Magnetic Fishing
potential_solutions.description: Remove the shoelaces from the sneakers and tie them together to make a long string. Tie one end securely around the heavy fridge magnet, then lower it down the vent to catch the keys.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: Sticky Plunge
potential_solutions.description: Chew a piece of gum until it is soft and sticky, then press it firmly onto the end of the metal tape measure. Lock the tape measure as you extend it down the vent, pressing the gum onto the keys to lift them out.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: Hook and Light
potential_solutions.description: Bend the wire clothes hanger into a long, straight piece of wire with a small hook at one end. Turn on the flashlight and aim it down the vent so you can see the keys, then use the wire hook to snag the key ring.

title: The Vent of No Return
complaint: Hi! I'm Emma. I am supposed to leave for a huge job interview that starts in 45 minutes, and I am already running late. I just accidentally dropped my only set of car keys down a narrow, deep air vent in my hallway floor, and the grate is stuck so my hands are too big to reach them!
on_hand_items: a pair of running shoes with long shoelaces

clue_cards.title: Magnetic Attraction
clue_cards.insight: Car keys always have a metal ring. Look for something nearby that naturally sticks to metal, and find a way to lower it down the gap.

clue_cards.title: Sticky Extension
clue_cards.insight: If your arms aren't long enough, you need to build an extension. Tape can be wrapped inside out to grab things from afar.

clue_cards.title: Shape Shifting
clue_cards.insight: Some everyday objects are made of thin metal that can be untwisted and reshaped into a long, reaching hook.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Magnetic Plumb Line
potential_solutions.description: Take one shoelace out of the running shoes. Use a small piece of duct tape to attach the fridge magnet to the end of the shoelace. Drop the magnet down the vent holding the other end of the shoelace, let it click onto the key ring, and carefully pull the keys up.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: The Sticky Stick
potential_solutions.description: Wrap a generous amount of duct tape around one end of the wooden yardstick, making sure the sticky side is facing outward. Use the flashlight to see exactly where the keys are, then press the sticky end of the yardstick firmly onto the keys to lift them out.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Custom Hook
potential_solutions.description: Untwist and stretch out the wire coat hanger until it is one long piece of metal, leaving a small hook shape at the very end. Shine the flashlight down the hole to guide your hand, slide the wire down, snag the key ring with the hook, and fish the keys out.

title: The Grate Escape
complaint: Hi! I'm Lucas. My ride to the airport is honking outside and I have exactly five minutes to leave. I just accidentally dropped my apartment keys down a narrow, deep floor grate and I can't lock the door without them!
on_hand_items: a pair of running shoes with long laces

clue_cards.title: Magnetic Attraction
clue_cards.insight: Keys are almost always attached to a steel ring. A heavy magnet can grab them from a distance without needing perfect aim.

clue_cards.title: Going Fishing
clue_cards.insight: You need a long, flexible line that can drop straight down the narrow opening. Look at your footwear for a makeshift rope.

clue_cards.title: Sticky Reach
clue_cards.insight: If you need to reach deep into a tight space, something stiff and straight is necessary. Wrapping tape backwards makes a great sticky grabber.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: Magnetic Fishing Line
potential_solutions.description: Pull the long laces out of the running shoes and tie them together to make one long string. Tie the fridge magnet securely to the bottom of the laces. Shine the flashlight down the grate to spot the keys, then lower the magnet down to snap onto the metal key ring and pull it up.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: The Sticky Measuring Tape
potential_solutions.description: Pull out a long section of the metal tape measure and lock it so it stays stiff. Tear off a piece of duct tape and wrap it inside out around the end of the tape measure so the sticky side faces out. Lower the rigid tape measure down the grate and press the sticky end firmly against the keys to lift them out.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Wire Hook
potential_solutions.description: Untwist the wire coat hanger and bend it out into a single, long straight wire. Use the pliers or your hands to form a small, tight hook at one end. Shine the flashlight down into the grate, lower the hook, and carefully loop it through the key ring to fish the keys back to the surface.

title: The Purple Juice Panic
complaint: Hi! I'm Mia. I'm sitting in the school cafeteria waiting for the science fair to start, and my best friend Sam just spilled bright purple grape juice all over his white shirt! He is about to cry because he has to present his project next, and I need to figure out a way to help him handle this politely without drawing a huge crowd and embarrassing him.

clue_cards.title: Keep It Private
clue_cards.insight: When a friend is embarrassed by a mistake, giving them a private space to fix it helps them calm down without feeling like everyone is staring.

clue_cards.title: The Quick Cover-Up
clue_cards.insight: If a mess can't be cleaned up quickly, the most polite and stress-free thing to do is cover it up so your friend can confidently get back to their day.

clue_cards.title: Distract and Deflect
clue_cards.insight: People will only notice a mistake if it's the most interesting thing to look at. Giving the audience something brighter and cooler to focus on takes the pressure off your friend!

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Privacy Shield
potential_solutions.description: Mia stands the large cardboard poster board up on the cafeteria table to create a temporary wall. While the other kids can't see, she hands Sam the oversized school sweatshirt to put on over his stained shirt. He gets to change privately and goes to his presentation feeling comfortable and confident.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: The VIP Badge
potential_solutions.description: Using the dry-erase marker, Mia writes 'CHIEF SCIENTIST' on the blank paper name tag. She places the shiny foil sticker on it to make it look official. She then uses a piece of masking tape to stick the giant badge directly over the juice stain on Sam's shirt, completely hiding it while making him look important.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Distraction Technique
potential_solutions.description: Mia uses the plain water and paper napkins to quietly dab away the worst of the juice puddle so it stops dripping. Then, she cuts out a cool shape from the masking tape with the scissors, puts it on the front of his large cardboard poster board, and has him hold the poster up high across his chest as he walks to the fair. Everyone looks at his amazing sign instead of his shirt!

title: The Spinach Situation
complaint: Hi! I'm Benjamin. I'm sitting at a crowded cafeteria table having lunch with my friends, but there is a big problem. My best friend Tommy has a huge piece of green spinach stuck right in his front teeth, and I need to let him know without making him feel totally embarrassed in front of everyone.
on_hand_items: a pack of mint chewing gum

clue_cards.title: Silent Messages
clue_cards.insight: You can communicate a secret message to a friend without saying anything out loud, keeping the rest of the table from finding out.

clue_cards.title: Self-Discovery
clue_cards.insight: If you give someone a way to see their own face, they might notice the problem all by themselves without you having to point it out.

clue_cards.title: A Helpful Distraction
clue_cards.insight: Offering someone something new to eat, drink, or chew can naturally help clear away leftover food bits from their mouth.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Secret Note
potential_solutions.description: Use the red marker to write a quick, polite warning on the blank sticky note. Fold it up inside the paper napkin and hand it directly to Tommy so only he sees the message.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: The Casual Reflection
potential_solutions.description: Pretend to look at your own teeth using the pocket mirror or the back of the shiny metal spoon. Then, casually hand it to Tommy and ask if he wants to see his funny reflection, allowing him to spot the spinach himself.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Gum Swap
potential_solutions.description: Offer Tommy a piece from the pack of mint chewing gum and slide the unopened juice box his way. Chewing the gum and taking a drink will naturally unstick the spinach from his teeth without anyone ever mentioning it.

title: The Spinach Smile
complaint: Hi! I'm Amelia. I am waiting in line for school pictures with my friend Sam. Sam has a huge piece of green spinach stuck right in his front teeth, and I need to let him know to clean it before his picture is taken without embarrassing him in front of the whole class!

clue_cards.title: Visual Cues
clue_cards.insight: Sometimes showing someone what they look like is easier and kinder than saying a problem out loud.

clue_cards.title: Secret Messages
clue_cards.insight: Writing a quick note can keep a secret just between two friends without anyone else hearing.

clue_cards.title: Sharing a Solution
clue_cards.insight: Offering a friend something that naturally cleans teeth helps them fix the problem on their own without feeling called out.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: Direct Action
potential_solutions.description: Pretend to check your own hair and smile using the small pocket mirror. Then, casually hand it to Sam and ask if he wants to check his smile before the photo. He will see the spinach and wipe it away himself with the paper tissue.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: Environmental Adaptation
potential_solutions.description: Use the blue crayon to draw a smile with a dot on the teeth on the blank sticky note. Stick the note secretly inside his yellow school folder and point to it so only he sees your hidden warning message.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: Lateral Swap
potential_solutions.description: Offer Sam a drink from the plastic water bottle and the stick of peppermint gum, telling him you both should 'freshen up' before the camera flashes. The water and gum will naturally wash the spinach away.

title: The Mushroom Haircut Mishap
complaint: Hi! I'm James. I'm at my best friend Leo's house for a playdate, but I accidentally said his new haircut makes him look like a mushroom, and now he's sad and hiding inside his cardboard fort and won't talk to me!
on_hand_items: a piece of blank printer paper
a handful of plastic googly eyes
a pair of blunt safety scissors
a small bag of gummy bears

clue_cards.title: Give Them Space
clue_cards.insight: When someone is upset, forcing them to talk right away can make it worse. Leaving a kind message lets them read it when they are ready.

clue_cards.title: The Peace Offering
clue_cards.insight: Sharing a favorite treat or lending them something you really like shows that you care about their feelings and want to be friends again.

clue_cards.title: Break the Ice Gently
clue_cards.insight: Sometimes a little bit of soft, friendly humor can help someone stop feeling embarrassed and start smiling again.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Slide-Under Apology
potential_solutions.description: Use the blank printer paper and the box of colorful crayons to draw a nice picture of you and Leo playing together. Write a big 'I'm Sorry!' on it, and gently slide the paper under the wall of the cardboard fort so he can accept your apology without feeling pressured to come out right away.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: The Apology Puppet
potential_solutions.description: Use the brown paper lunch bag, glue stick, and plastic googly eyes to build a silly hand puppet. Put the puppet on your hand, lightly tap on the fort, and have the puppet give a very gentle, funny apology to make Leo smile and break the awkward silence.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Snack Treaty
potential_solutions.description: Set up the fruit punch juice box, the bag of gummy bears, and your favorite action figure toy right outside the entrance of the fort. Announce that you brought a peace offering for him, then step back and give him space to come out and share the snacks when he feels better.

title: The Spinach Situation
complaint: Hi! I'm Harper. I am sitting at the crowded lunch table with my best friend. The problem is, she has a huge piece of green spinach stuck in her front teeth and is about to talk to the new kid, but I don't want to embarrass her by pointing it out loud!
on_hand_items: a slightly crushed bag of chips

clue_cards.title: Private Message
clue_cards.insight: Sometimes the nicest way to share embarrassing news is to not say a single word. Is there a way to pass her a secret warning?

clue_cards.title: Self-Discovery
clue_cards.insight: People feel a lot less embarrassed if they notice the food in their teeth all by themselves. What items can show a reflection?

clue_cards.title: The Distraction Drop
clue_cards.insight: Creating a small, harmless distraction gives you a quick chance to get close to your friend and whisper privately.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Secret Note
potential_solutions.description: Use the thick black marker to write a quick warning on a page from the blank sticky note pad. Hide the note under the folded paper napkin and slide it across the table to her so only she sees it.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: The Casual Reflection
potential_solutions.description: Take out the compact pocket mirror or the shiny metal spoon and pretend to check your own teeth. Then, casually hand it to her and ask her if she wants to check hers, letting her see the spinach herself.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Distraction Drop
potential_solutions.description: Accidentally-on-purpose knock the empty plastic water bottle or plastic lunch tray onto the floor. When you both bend down under the table to pick it up, quickly whisper the warning in her ear where no one else can hear.

title: The Chatty Cubicle
complaint: Hi! I'm Alexander. I'm working at my open-plan office desk trying to finish a massive report, but my extremely talkative neighbor keeps interrupting me every two minutes to chat about their weekend.
on_hand_items: a pad of yellow sticky notes

clue_cards.title: Power of Non-Verbal Boundaries
clue_cards.insight: Sometimes, the most polite way to tell someone you are busy is to not use words at all. Visual cues can do the heavy lifting for you.

clue_cards.title: The Peace Offering
clue_cards.insight: Offering a small gift or snack can soften the blow when you need to shut down a conversation. It shows you still value the person even if you can't chat right now.

clue_cards.title: Shift the Environment
clue_cards.insight: People read the room based on lighting and sound. Making your workspace look and sound like an intense focus zone will subconsciously discourage interruptions.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: Direct Action
potential_solutions.description: Put on the over-ear headphones to visually signal you are busy. Use the black permanent marker to write 'On a tight deadline!' on a yellow sticky note, and stick it to the back of your bright red cardboard folder propped up against your coffee mug. This creates a clear, polite visual boundary.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: Environmental Adaptation
potential_solutions.description: Turn on the small electric desktop fan to create a gentle wall of white noise between your desks. Angle the small desk lamp directly down onto your workspace and lean in. This closed-off body language and focused lighting subtly tells your neighbor that the chatting window has closed.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: Lateral Swap
potential_solutions.description: Hand your neighbor the bag of mixed nuts as a friendly peace offering. While doing so, smile and politely say you have to go completely off the grid to finish your report. The snack gives them something positive to focus on while you establish a firm work boundary.

title: The Dinner Debate Disaster
complaint: Hi! I'm Evelyn. I am hosting a small dinner party in my dining room to introduce my old friends to some new neighbors, but two of the guests are locked in a heated, uncomfortable debate that is making everyone else awkwardly silent and ruining the evening.

clue_cards.title: The Host's Interruption
clue_cards.insight: Serving food or drinks is a polite, natural way to physically interrupt a conversation without seeming confrontational or taking sides.

clue_cards.title: Shift the Focus
clue_cards.insight: When a conversation goes sour, introducing a sudden, structured group activity can quickly force everyone's attention onto a new, neutral topic.

clue_cards.title: Break the Sightline
clue_cards.insight: People find it much harder to argue when they cannot make direct eye contact. A physical barrier can subtly defuse tension.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Hospitality Block
potential_solutions.description: Grab the plate of warm appetizers, the bottle of wine, and the corkscrew. Walk directly over to the arguing guests, physically stepping into their space to enthusiastically offer food and pour drinks. This forces them to pause their debate to interact with you, effectively breaking the momentum of the argument so you can change the subject.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: The Forced Icebreaker
potential_solutions.description: Pass out the paper napkins and the ballpoint pen. Place the large serving bowl in the middle of the table and announce a sudden party game where everyone must write down a funny secret or silly question. Set the digital kitchen timer for one minute to rush everyone into participating, instantly redirecting the room's energy away from the awkward debate.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Centerpiece Reset
potential_solutions.description: Pick up the large decorative houseplant. Pretend you need to clear off a side table and casually place the bulky plant directly in the center of the dining table, right between the two arguing guests. The sudden physical barrier breaks their direct eye contact, making it highly awkward for them to keep shouting at each other.

title: The Embarrassing Anecdote
complaint: Hi! I'm Daniel. I'm hosting a small dinner party with my strict new boss and some coworkers, but my best friend just started telling a highly embarrassing story about my wild college days, and I need a subtle way to interrupt the conversation and change the subject before my professional reputation is ruined!

clue_cards.title: The Art of the Oops
clue_cards.insight: A harmless, minor accident is one of the most effective ways to instantly reset a group's focus and derail a story without seeming intentionally rude.

clue_cards.title: Digital Bailout
clue_cards.insight: Sometimes the best way to interrupt someone politely is to let a sudden, loud notification do the interrupting for you.

clue_cards.title: Overzealous Hosting
clue_cards.insight: You can abruptly change the topic by suddenly shifting your energy toward being an aggressively attentive and loud host regarding the meal.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Clumsy Diversion
potential_solutions.description: Reach across the table and 'accidentally' knock over the glass tumbler with the metal spoon, then immediately toss the cloth napkin over it. The sudden noise and minor spill force everyone to pause and help clean up, effectively killing the story's momentum so you can pivot to a safer topic.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: The Phantom Call
potential_solutions.description: Secretly use your smartphone under the table to set an alarm for ten seconds. When it loudly rings, feign surprise, apologize to your boss for the 'urgent' interruption, and use the moment to completely reset the conversation when you pretend to decline the call.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Culinary Interruption
potential_solutions.description: Grab the wooden pepper grinder and the bottle of hot sauce, enthusiastically stand up, and loudly offer to season your friend's food right at that moment. The sudden, overly hospitable gesture and physical intrusion into their space shifts the spotlight entirely back to the food.

title: The Heated Debate
complaint: Hi! I'm Abigail. I'm hosting a small dinner party for my closest friends, but two of them have started a heated, awkward argument about a recent movie. The rest of the guests are staring at their plates in silence, and I need a polite, subtle way to break the tension and change the subject before the night is ruined.
on_hand_items: a bag of whole coffee beans

clue_cards.title: Clue 1: Break the Momentum
clue_cards.insight: When people are stuck in a tense argument, a sudden but harmless distraction like a flash of light or a sharp, unexpected noise can reset their attention without you having to say a word.

clue_cards.title: Clue 2: The Power of a Favor
clue_cards.insight: Asking an arguing guest to help you with a physical task in another room separates the debaters and makes the helper feel valued rather than scolded.

clue_cards.title: Clue 3: Shift to Play
clue_cards.insight: Introducing a structured group activity with physical props gives people a socially acceptable excuse to drop an embarrassing argument without losing face.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Flash Distraction
potential_solutions.description: Walk right up to the arguing pair, smile brightly, and use the Polaroid camera to take a sudden flash picture of them. The surprise of the flash and the sound of the physical photo printing will immediately stop their momentum. Hand them the photo and ask them to sign it for a party guestbook, shifting their focus to a shared, lighthearted task.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: The Clumsy Interruption
potential_solutions.description: Accidentally-on-purpose drop the metal spoon loudly into the empty ceramic serving bowl. The sudden clatter will naturally pause their conversation. Use that brief moment of silence to pull out the bag of whole coffee beans and politely ask one of the arguers if they wouldn't mind coming to the kitchen to help you grind them, physically separating the pair.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Urgent Game Pivot
potential_solutions.description: Bring out the deck of playing cards and the digital kitchen timer. Announce enthusiastically that it's time for a speed-round card game. Set the timer for two minutes to create a sense of fun urgency. The loud beep of the timer and the act of dealing cards forces everyone to look at their hands and disengage from the debate.

title: The Overheard Rant
complaint: Hi! I'm Henry. I am at my firm's annual holiday cocktail party. My coworker is loudly complaining about our boss, completely unaware that the boss's spouse is standing right behind them, and I need to discreetly stop this disaster without causing a scene!

clue_cards.title: A Slight Distraction
clue_cards.insight: Spilling or dropping something minor can immediately shift someone's focus and stop a conversation dead in its tracks without causing offense.

clue_cards.title: Visual Cues
clue_cards.insight: Writing a quick note on something inconspicuous can pass an urgent message without the surrounding people hearing a word.

clue_cards.title: The Food Pivot
clue_cards.insight: Offering someone a bite to eat forces a physical pause in their speaking and provides a very natural way to change the subject.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Appetizer Interruption
potential_solutions.description: Walk right up to the coworker with the small plate of appetizers and the decorative toothpick. Loudly and enthusiastically insist they try the food immediately, forcing them to pause their rant to chew, and use that window to change the conversation topic to the catering.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: The Covert Note
potential_solutions.description: Use the ballpoint pen to scribble 'Turn around!' on the back of the blank business card. Walk over, interrupt politely by saying you have that contact info they asked for, and hand them the card. They will read the cue and stop talking.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The 'Accidental' Splash
potential_solutions.description: Step toward them and pretend to trip on the dropped cloth napkin, deliberately splashing a little bit of the glass of ice water near their shoes. Rush to clean it up with the paper cocktail napkin, which will completely derail their complaining and give you an excuse to pull them aside.

title: The Trapped Tin
complaint: Hi! I'm Ella. I'm searching my room for the next mystery clue which is hidden inside a small metal mint tin, but it accidentally slipped deep behind my heavy wooden bookshelf and I can't reach it!
on_hand_items: a pair of sneakers with long shoelaces

clue_cards.title: Look in the Dark
clue_cards.insight: It is really dark behind that heavy bookshelf. You might need to use something bright to spot exactly where the clue fell first.

clue_cards.title: Magnetic Magic
clue_cards.insight: The mystery clue is inside a metal tin. Is there an item nearby that naturally sticks to certain types of metal?

clue_cards.title: Going Fishing
clue_cards.insight: If your arm can't reach all the way down, you need to make something longer. You can tape things together to make a long pole, or tie things together to make a fishing line.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: Magnet Fishing
potential_solutions.description: Take the long shoelaces out of the sneakers and tie them together to make a long string. Tie one end of your string tightly around the fridge magnet. Lower the magnet behind the bookshelf until it clicks onto the metal mint tin, then pull it up!

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: The Sticky Stick
potential_solutions.description: Use the sticky tape to attach the plastic drinking straw to the end of the wooden ruler to make it longer. Roll a piece of sticky tape backward so the sticky side is facing out, put it on the end of the straw, and reach down to grab the tin.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Magnet Wand
potential_solutions.description: Turn on the small flashlight and drop it down into the shoe box on the floor pointing toward the crack, so you have both hands free and can see. Tape the fridge magnet to the very end of the wooden ruler, then reach down with the ruler to snap the magnet onto the tin and lift it out.

title: The Case of the Dropped Coin
complaint: Hi! I'm Sebastian. I am in my treehouse detective agency trying to solve a huge mystery. But I just dropped our most important clue, a shiny metal secret code coin, down a deep crack in the floorboards and my fingers can't reach it!
on_hand_items: a pair of sneakers with long shoelaces

clue_cards.title: Magnetic Pull
clue_cards.insight: Metal objects like your secret code coin will easily stick to magnetic things.

clue_cards.title: Sticky Situation
clue_cards.insight: If a clue is just out of reach, you might be able to use a long tool with something sticky on the end to grab it.

clue_cards.title: Hook and Pull
clue_cards.insight: Some thin metal items can be bent and shaped into tools for scooping or hooking.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Magnet Drop
potential_solutions.description: Take a shoelace out of one of the sneakers and tie it tightly around the fridge magnet. Lower the magnet down into the crack until it clicks onto the metal coin, then carefully pull it up.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: The Sticky Stick
potential_solutions.description: Chew the wad of gum until it is nice and soft, then press it onto the end of the wooden ruler. Poke the ruler down into the floorboards and press the gum firmly against the coin to lift it out.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Wire Scoop
potential_solutions.description: Untwist and bend the wire clothes hanger until it forms a long, straight rod with a small hook at the very end. Slide the wire hook down the crack to scoop underneath the coin and pull it back to the surface.

title: The Bookcase Clue
complaint: Hi! I'm Scarlett. I'm searching my grandpa's study for the final piece of our family scavenger hunt, but the paper clue just slipped right underneath a heavy oak bookcase and my arm is too short to reach it!
on_hand_items: a pair of sneakers with long shoelaces

clue_cards.title: Sticky Situation
clue_cards.insight: If your fingers can't reach the paper, maybe you can make a long tool grab it for you by adding a sticky surface to the end.

clue_cards.title: Light the Way
clue_cards.insight: It is hard to fish for a clue in the dark shadows! Make sure you can see exactly where the paper is hiding before you try to grab it.

clue_cards.title: The Bendable Arm
clue_cards.insight: You have a large metal item in your pile that can be untwisted and stretched out into a very long, straight hook or poker.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Sticky Ruler
potential_solutions.description: Wrap some double-sided tape around one end of the long wooden ruler. Slide the ruler under the bookcase until it touches the paper clue, press down lightly, and pull it back out to safely retrieve the clue.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: Gum on a Wire
potential_solutions.description: Untwist the plain metal coat hanger to make a long, straight wire. Chew a piece of gum until it is sticky, put it on the tip of the wire, and use the flashlight to guide the sticky end right onto the paper clue to drag it out.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Side Sweeper
potential_solutions.description: Turn on the flashlight and lay it flat on the floor to light up the dark space under the bookcase. Slide the unbent metal coat hanger or the long wooden ruler all the way behind the paper clue, and carefully sweep it sideways until it pops out from under the edge of the furniture.

title: The Case of the Fallen Clue
complaint: Hi! I'm Jack. I am playing a detective game in my living room, but the final shiny metal clue fell right behind the heavy bookcase! I can't reach it, and the gap is too narrow for my arm to fit inside.
on_hand_items: a pair of sneakers with long shoelaces

clue_cards.title: The Power of Metal
clue_cards.insight: The mystery clue is made of shiny metal. Certain objects from your kitchen might love to stick to it naturally!

clue_cards.title: Sticky Situations
clue_cards.insight: If you can't grab something with your fingers, something sticky on the end of a long, flat tool could pick it up for you.

clue_cards.title: Shape Shifting
clue_cards.insight: Some everyday items in your closet are made of soft metal that can be bent and unbent into a long reaching hook.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Magnetic Fishing Line
potential_solutions.description: Take one of the shoelaces out of the sneakers and tie it tightly around the fridge magnet. Drop the magnet down the gap behind the bookcase until it clicks onto the metal clue, then pull it up like you're fishing!

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: The Sticky Grabber
potential_solutions.description: Peel off a piece of double-sided tape and stick it to the very end of the wooden ruler. Slide the ruler down behind the bookcase, press the sticky end firmly against the clue, and lift it out.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Hook and Look
potential_solutions.description: Turn on the small pocket flashlight and shine it down the gap so you can see exactly where the clue is. Then, bend the wire clothes hanger into a long, straight rod with a hook at the bottom to snag the clue and pull it up.

title: The Floorboard Phantom
complaint: Hi! I'm Grace. I am in my backyard treehouse trying to solve a secret club mystery, but the most important piece of paper with the final clue just slipped through a narrow crack in the floorboards, and my fingers are too big to reach it!
on_hand_items: a pair of sneakers with shoelaces

clue_cards.title: Sticky Situations
clue_cards.insight: If you cannot grab something with your fingers, maybe you can use something gooey to make it stick to a long tool.

clue_cards.title: Going Fishing

clue_cards.insight: Some items can change shape. If you bend metal wire the right way, it can become a helpful tool for hooking or scooping round objects out of tight spots.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: Magnetic Fishing
potential_solutions.description: Take a long shoelace out of one of the sneakers and tie it tightly around the fridge magnet. Drop the magnet down the crack behind the bookshelf until it clicks onto the metal marble, then pull it up like a fishing pole.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: The Sticky Ruler
potential_solutions.description: Take the roll of masking tape and wrap a piece around the end of the wooden ruler with the sticky side facing out. Slide the ruler down the crack until it touches the marble, press firmly so the marble sticks to the tape, and lift it out.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: Wire Hook and Light
potential_solutions.description: Turn on the flashlight and shine it down the crack so you can see exactly where the marble is. Then, bend the wire coat hanger into a long, straight shape with a tiny hook at the end to gently scoop the marble back up to the top.

title: The Secret Fort Messenger
complaint: Hi! I'm Gabriel. I am building a massive pillow fort in my bedroom, but I need a way to send secret messages to my sister outside. The problem is the only gap is a tiny tunnel at the bottom, and I don't want to crawl out every time to hand her a note!
on_hand_items: a pair of sneakers with long shoelaces

clue_cards.title: Rolling Delivery
clue_cards.insight: Think about things that can move on their own. Is there something with wheels that could carry a piece of paper through a tunnel?

clue_cards.title: Pull and Retrieve
clue_cards.insight: If you take the strings out of your shoes, you get a really long line. How could a long line help you pull a message back and forth?

clue_cards.title: Magnetic Attraction
clue_cards.insight: Magnets stick to metal objects. If a piece of paper had something metal on it, you could drag it across the floor!

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Toy Car Courier
potential_solutions.description: Rip a piece of paper from your small notebook, write your message, and use the masking tape to stick it to the top of the toy remote control car. Drive the car through the tunnel to deliver the note without ever leaving the fort.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: The Shoelace Conveyor Belt
potential_solutions.description: Take the long shoelaces out of your sneakers and tie them together to make one big string. Tape one end of the string to your folded note. Toss the note through the tunnel to your sister, and she can pull the string back to send a reply!

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Magnetic Drag
potential_solutions.description: Slide the metal paperclip onto your written note and toss it out the tunnel. Tie a shoelace to your fridge magnet. When your sister writes back and slides the paperclip back onto the paper, you can throw the magnet out the tunnel to catch the paperclip and drag the note back in.

title: The Trapped Toy Robot
complaint: Hi! I'm Isaac. I am building a super secret invention in my treehouse lab, but my lucky metal toy robot just fell down a really skinny crack in the floorboards and my fingers won't fit to grab it!
on_hand_items: a pair of sneakers with long shoelaces
a piece of wrapped chewing gum

clue_cards.title: Metal Finder
clue_cards.insight: Your toy robot is made of metal. Is there something nearby that naturally sticks to metal objects?

clue_cards.title: Going Fishing
clue_cards.insight: If the crack is too deep for your fingers, you might need a way to lower something down like a fishing line.

clue_cards.title: Sticky Stick
clue_cards.insight: Tape and chewed gum are great for grabbing lightweight things. How can you make them reach far down into the floorboards?

potential_solutions.title: Magnet Fishing
potential_solutions.description: Take a shoelace out of the sneakers and tie it tightly around the fridge magnet. Lower the magnet down the crack until it clicks onto the metal robot, then carefully pull it up!

potential_solutions.title: The Sticky Ruler
potential_solutions.description: Chew the gum until it is soft and sticky, then press it onto the end of the wooden ruler. Poke the ruler into the crack and press the gum onto the toy robot to lift it out.

potential_solutions.title: Inside-Out Tape Trap
potential_solutions.description: Wrap a piece of masking tape around the unsharpened pencil with the sticky side facing out. Shine the flashlight into the crack so you can see, then poke the pencil down to stick the tape to the robot.

title: The Bookshelf Black Hole
complaint: Hi! I'm Willow. I am in my home office preparing for a huge creative pitch, but I just dropped my crucial USB drive down a deep, narrow gap behind my massive floor-to-ceiling bookshelf! The shelf is fully loaded and completely impossible to move, my arm cannot fit in the tight space, and I desperately need to retrieve that drive right now to finish my work.
on_hand_items: a pair of sneakers with long shoelaces

clue_cards.title: Extend Your Reach
clue_cards.insight: You have items that can stretch, unroll, or provide extra length. Look for something long enough to reach the floor behind the shelf.

clue_cards.title: Sticky Situations
clue_cards.insight: If you cannot physically grab the object with your hands, maybe you can make it stick to something else so you can pull it up.

clue_cards.title: Sweeping Angles
clue_cards.insight: Sometimes reaching from the top is too difficult. Think about combining items to create a tool that can sweep the drive out from the side gap.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Sticky Plumb Line
potential_solutions.description: Stick the piece of chewed bubblegum to the bottom tip of the metal tape measure. Shine the small flashlight down the gap to see the USB drive, extend the tape measure down until the gum presses firmly against the drive, and carefully reel it back up.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: The Makeshift Side-Rake
potential_solutions.description: Use the roll of duct tape to attach the rigid plastic ruler horizontally to the bottom of the long wooden broom. Slide this new L-shaped tool into the gap from the side of the bookshelf and sweep the USB drive out into the open.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Shoelace Snag
potential_solutions.description: Remove a shoelace from the sneakers and tie one end securely to the large binder clip. Use the roll of duct tape to lightly attach the shoelace along the rigid plastic ruler to guide the heavy clip down the narrow gap, hooking it onto the keychain loop of the USB drive before pulling it up.

title: The Top-Down Dilemma
complaint: Hi! I'm Character_57. I am in the basement innovation lab trying to record a top-down video of a new paper prototype. But I don't have a tripod, and my phone keeps sliding off the random objects I try to balance it on, ruining the shot!

clue_cards.title: Height and Weight
clue_cards.insight: You need something tall and sturdy for height, and something very heavy to act as an anchor so your makeshift stand doesn't tip over.

clue_cards.title: Bridging the Gap
clue_cards.insight: A flat, grated surface can act as a great camera platform because a phone can sit flat on top while the lens peeks through the wire gaps.

clue_cards.title: Grip and Secure
clue_cards.insight: If you use something adjustable, rubber and metal clips can pinch and hold a phone tightly to an existing frame.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Rack Bridge
potential_solutions.description: Place the ream of printer paper on the desk to create a tall base. Lay the metal cooling rack flat on top of the paper so that half of it hangs over the desk area. Place the heavy dictionary on the back of the rack to hold it down securely. Finally, lay your phone flat on the overhanging part of the rack with the camera pointing straight down through the wire grid.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: The Lamp Scaffold
potential_solutions.description: Position the adjustable desk lamp over your prototype area. Wrap the thick rubber band tightly around the lamp head and your phone to strap them together. Use the large metal binder clip to grip the edge of the phone to the rim of the lamp shade for extra security, giving you a fully adjustable, floating camera rig.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Jug Mount
potential_solutions.description: Use the scissors to cut the empty plastic milk jug in half. Cut a snug notch into the highest part of the plastic to wedge your phone into it vertically facing down. Use the duct tape to secure the bottom half of the jug to the desk or onto the ream of paper to give it enough height for a perfect overhead shot.

title: The Missing Screw
complaint: Hi! I'm Character_57. I'm in my garage workshop putting the final touches on my new prototype, but the very last custom metal screw just rolled off the table and fell into a deep, dark, narrow crack behind a heavy workbench that I cannot move.
on_hand_items: a pair of sneakers with shoelaces

clue_cards.title: Reaching the Depths
clue_cards.insight: You need something long and skinny to get down into the crack, and something to grab the screw once you reach the bottom.

clue_cards.title: Seeing the Unseen
clue_cards.insight: It is dark back there. You might need to bounce light or redirect your view to see exactly where the screw landed.

clue_cards.title: Sticky Situation
clue_cards.insight: Metal is naturally attracted to magnets, but if you can't use a magnet, anything with strong adhesive properties could pick up a lightweight screw.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: Magnetic Fishing Line
potential_solutions.description: Take a shoelace out of the sneakers and tie the fridge magnet to the end of it. Lower the magnet down into the crack until you hear it click onto the metal screw, then carefully pull it back up.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: Sticky Stick
potential_solutions.description: Use the scissors to cut a piece of double-sided tape and wrap it around the tip of the long wooden dowel. Shine the pocket flashlight down the crack to spot the screw, then press the sticky end of the dowel onto the screw to lift it out.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: Chewing Gum Hook
potential_solutions.description: Unbend the metal coat hanger into a long straight wire. Chew the gum until it is soft and stick it to the tip of the wire. Prop the makeup mirror over the crack and shine the flashlight into it to see the screw's reflection, then guide the gum-tipped wire down to grab it.

title: The Missing Pitch
complaint: Hi! I'm Character_57. I'm in the main prototyping studio trying to finish my model before the investor pitch, but the only plastic flash drive with my presentation on it slipped down an impossibly narrow gap behind this heavy, bolted-to-the-floor workbench!
on_hand_items: a spool of thin fishing line

clue_cards.title: Shedding Some Light
clue_cards.insight: You can't grab what you can't see. Try finding a way to bounce the beam of your light source down into that tight space.

clue_cards.title: Extend Your Reach
clue_cards.insight: Your arm is too thick to fit behind the bench. You need something thin, rigid, and long enough to reach the floor.

clue_cards.title: The Sticky Situation
clue_cards.insight: Since the flash drive is plastic, a magnet wouldn't work anyway. You need something tacky at the end of your reach-extender to grip the drive.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Sticky Stick
potential_solutions.description: Wrap some double-sided tape around the very end of the wooden yardstick. Slide the yardstick down the narrow gap, press the taped end firmly against the flash drive, and carefully pull it straight up.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: The Mirror and Gum Grab
potential_solutions.description: Chew the piece of gum until it is soft, then stick it to the end of the unbent wire coat hanger. Place the pocket mirror near the gap and shine the flashlight onto it to light up the dark space, allowing you to guide the sticky gum right onto the flash drive.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Snag and Drag
potential_solutions.description: Use the scissors to cut the wire coat hanger and bend a small hook into one piece. Tie the fishing line to the hooked wire, lower it down into the gap, and maneuver it to hook onto the flash drive's keychain loop to pull it up.

title: The Missing Prototype Pin
complaint: Hi! I'm Character_57. I am in my home workshop setting up for a major video pitch to show off my new invention. The problem is, the crucial metal pin that holds the prototype together just rolled off the table and fell down the narrow, dark gap behind my massive, immovable workbench, and my pitch starts in five minutes!
on_hand_items: a pair of work boots with long laces

clue_cards.title: Magnetic Reach
clue_cards.insight: Magnets are great for picking up metal, but you need a way to lower the magnet into a tight space. Look for a long, flexible string-like item you can tie to it.

clue_cards.title: Sticky Situation
clue_cards.insight: If you need precision, a rigid pole with something sticky on the end might work better than a swinging magnet. How can you extend your reach?

clue_cards.title: Guiding the Way
clue_cards.insight: It is hard to see down a narrow gap. You might need to use a stiff metal item as an extending arm that can carry another item down to the floor.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Magnetic Pendulum
potential_solutions.description: Remove the long laces from the work boots and tie one tightly around the heavy-duty fridge magnet. Shine the flashlight down the gap to spot the missing pin, then lower the magnet down by the lace until it grabs the metal pin so you can pull it back up.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: The Tape Measure Crane
potential_solutions.description: Pull out a long section of the metal tape measure and lock it in place. Stick the fridge magnet directly to the metal tip of the tape measure (it will hold on its own). Use the rigid tape measure to reach down the gap and sweep the magnet across the floor until it catches the pin.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Sticky Extension
potential_solutions.description: Unbend the wire coat hanger into a long, straight rod. Wrap a piece of double-sided tape (or a chewed piece of chewing gum) around the very tip. Lower the wire down the gap, press the sticky end firmly onto the metal pin, and carefully lift it out.
